name: Finding hidden features in neural networks
gist: Modern AI models hide their processing in millions of dimensions. These papers find tiny subsets of those dimensions that do meaningful work, using sparse autoencoders and other dictionary-learning approaches.
explain: Neural networks store information in compressed form. A language model might encode 'this word means cat' not in one neuron but in a pattern spread across hundreds of them, like a code written in a high-dimensional space. Researchers want to find the 'atoms' of this code — the minimal set of directions in that space where each one stands for one clear concept. If they can do that, the model becomes much easier to understand: instead of millions of adjustable numbers, they focus on a few interpretable features.

The challenge is that finding these features is like recovering the original message from heavily scrambled data. The model's learned representation might mix multiple concepts in subtle ways. A direction might matter only in certain contexts. And some features might be quirks of the training process, not real patterns the model should use. These papers use dictionary learning and sparse autoencoders — techniques that find a small set of direction vectors (directions in the high-dimensional space) that can reconstruct the model's hidden states while staying interpretable. The goal is to decompose the model into a 'parts list' that a human can reason about.

papers.title: Can SAEs reveal and mitigate racial biases of LLMs in healthcare?
papers.contribution: Identifies SAE latents correlating with race; demonstrates that steering via latents can induce problematic associations and offers potential for bias mitigation in controlled settings.

papers.title: Correlations in the Data Lead to Semantically Rich Feature Geometry Under Superposition
papers.contribution: Shows semantically clustered representations and ordered circles emerge from linear superposition under compression, revealing how language models achieve rich feature geometry.

papers.title: DB-KSVD: Scalable Alternating Optimization for Disentangling High-Dimensional Embedding Spaces
papers.contribution: DB-KSVD achieves competitive results on SAEBench benchmarks for disentangling embeddings in Gemma-2-2B, Pythia-160M, and vision models like DINOv2.

papers.title: Dimensional Collapse in Transformer Attention Outputs: A Challenge for Sparse Dictionary Learning
papers.contribution: Reduces dead features from 87% to below 1% in 1M-feature Attention Output SAEs and demonstrates the approach extends to other sparse dictionary learning methods.

papers.title: Evolution of Concepts in Language Model Pre-Training
papers.contribution: The analysis reveals a two-stage process: statistical learning followed by feature learning, with causal connections between feature evolution and downstream performance.

papers.title: HARP: Hallucination Detection via Reasoning Subspace Projection
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art AUROC of 92.8% on TriviaQA, outperforming the previous best by 7.5%, while reducing feature dimension to ~5% of original.

papers.title: Internal Planning in Language Models: Characterizing Horizon and Branch Awareness
papers.contribution: The analysis reveals planning properties in language models across synthetic grammar, path-finding, and natural language tasks, advancing understanding of how models structure intermediate computations for coherent generation.

papers.title: Into the Rabbit Hull: From Task-Relevant Concepts in DINO to Minkowski Geometry
papers.contribution: Reveals functional specialization in task recruitment (classification uses learned negations, segmentation uses boundary detectors, depth uses monocular cues), antipodal concept pairs, and distributed encoding.

papers.title: Mechanism of Task-oriented Information Removal in In-context Learning
papers.contribution: Identifies Denoising Heads enabling task-oriented information removal; ablation experiments blocking removal operation show ICL accuracy degrades significantly, confirming the critical role of information removal.

papers.title: Taming Polysemanticity in LLMs: Theory-Grounded Feature Recovery via Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Develops Group Bias Adaptation (GBA) variant with superior performance on LLMs up to 2B parameters and provides first SAE algorithm with theoretical recovery guarantees.

papers.title: Uncertainty as Feature Gaps: Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification of LLMs in Contextual Question-Answering
papers.contribution: The method substantially outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised and supervised uncertainty quantification approaches on multiple QA benchmarks in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings.

papers.title: A Behavioural and Representational Evaluation of Goal-Directedness in Language Model Agents
papers.contribution: Shows that LLM agents encode coarse spatial maps preserving task-relevant cues and that their actions are consistent with these representations; reasoning reorganizes them from spatial cues to action selection.

papers.title: AbsTopK: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders For Bidirectional Features
papers.contribution: Improves reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, enabling single features to encode contrasting concepts, matching or exceeding supervised Difference-in-Mean approach.

papers.title: ActivationReasoning: Logical Reasoning in Latent Activation Spaces
papers.contribution: Scales robustly with reasoning complexity, generalizes to abstract tasks, transfers across models, and improves transparency and reliable control.

papers.title: AdaSCALE: Adaptive Scaling for OOD Detection
papers.contribution: AdaSCALE achieves state-of-the-art OOD detection, outperforming OptFS by 14.94% in near-OOD and 21.28% in far-OOD settings on ImageNet-1k.

papers.title: At the Edge of Understanding: Sparse Autoencoders Trace The Limits of Transformer Generalization
papers.contribution: Quantifies distributional shifts and provides a diagnostic framework for understanding transformer robustness at inference time.

papers.title: Automated Interpretability Metrics Do Not Distinguish Trained and Random Transformers
papers.contribution: Many SAE quality metrics and auto-interpretability scores produce similar results for trained and random models, showing these metrics alone do not guarantee learned, computationally relevant features.

papers.title: Base Models Know How to Reason, Thinking Models Learn When
papers.contribution: Reveals RL primarily teaches models when to apply pre-existing capabilities while SFT teaches new mechanisms; implications for efficient reasoning model development.

papers.title: Breaking the Block: Preserving Data Continuity to Train Superior SAEs for Instruct Models
papers.contribution: Achieves significantly lower MSE (0.6468 vs 5.1985), 21.1% high-quality features, and enables fine-grained control through special token interventions.

papers.title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that C$^2$R effectively mitigates both splitting and absorption while, crucially, preserving reconstruction fidelity, providing a principled solution that enhance

papers.title: Causal Interpretation of Neural Network Computations with Contribution Decomposition (CODEC)
papers.contribution: Decomposes network behavior into interpretable contribution modes that grow in sparsity across layers and enable control of intermediate layers while maintaining output fidelity.

papers.title: Concepts' Information Bottleneck Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms vanilla CBM counterparts across six CBM families and three benchmarks, improving both predictive performance and reliability of concept-level interventions.

papers.title: CorrSteer: Generation-Time LLM Steering via Correlated Sparse Autoencoder Features
papers.contribution: Achieves +3.3% on MMLU and +27.1% on HarmBench with lower side-effects than fine-tuning, scaling to 10^5 SAE features via streaming correlation.

papers.title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: They demonstrate that SAE insertion in DLMs reduces cross-entropy loss in early layers (unlike autoregressive LLMs where it incurs a penalty) and that SAE features enable more effective DLM steering and decoding order prediction.

papers.title: DNA: Uncovering Universal Latent Forgery Knowledge
papers.contribution: Achieves superior detection even under few-shot conditions with remarkable robustness across architectures and unseen generative models.

papers.title: Diagnosing Multi-step Reasoning Failures in Black-box LLMs via Stepwise Confidence Attribution
papers.contribution: Identifies low-confidence steps strongly correlated with reasoning errors, improving self-correction success rate by up to 13.5% over answer-level feedback through step-guided interventions.

papers.title: Differential syntactic and semantic encoding in LLMs
papers.contribution: Finds syntax and semantics are partially linearly encoded in DeepSeek-V3 with different cross-layer profiles, enabling selective decoupling of linguistic signals.

papers.title: Discovering and Steering Interpretable Concepts in Large Generative Music Models
papers.contribution: The method reveals both familiar musical concepts and coherent uncodified patterns, and concepts can be steered to control model generation.

papers.title: Disentangling Geometry, Performance, and Training in Language Models
papers.contribution: High effective rank correlates with best performance but trend is not universal; effective rank primarily reflects training choices like batch size and weight decay rather than performance.

papers.title: Do LLMs Signal When They’re Right? Evidence from Neuron Agreement
papers.contribution: NAD matches majority voting on benchmarks with verifiable answers and outperforms Avg@64 on open-ended coding tasks, reducing token usage by 99% with minimal quality loss via early stopping.

papers.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Identify Reasoning Features in Language Models?
papers.contribution: Finds 45-90% of candidates are sensitive to token-level interventions and LLM-guided falsification triggers non-reasoning inputs that suppress activation of many supposedly reasoning features.

papers.title: Domain Restriction via SAE Multi-Layer Transitions
papers.contribution: SAE layer transitions exhibit great capability in distinguishing OOD texts across gemma-2 2B and 9B models with interpretable internal evolution analysis.

papers.title: Emergent Misalignment is Easy, Narrow Misalignment is Hard
papers.contribution: General misalignment is more stable, efficient, and robust than narrow solution, providing basis for monitoring and mitigation.

papers.title: Emotions Where Art Thou: Understanding and Characterizing the Emotional Latent Space of Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Reveals universal emotional subspace stable across languages and domains, enabling manipulation of internal emotion perception while preserving semantics.

papers.title: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models
papers.contribution: Identified 26 off-topic detector latents and demonstrated that zero-ablating them reduces multi-attempt rate by 25%, and that ESR can be deliberately controlled through prompting (5× increase) and fine-tuning.

papers.title: Ensembling Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Compared to expanded SAEs with equivalent feature count, ensembles improve activation reconstruction and achieve better performance on concept detection and spurious correlation removal.

papers.title: Evaluating SAE interpretability without generating explanations
papers.contribution: Provides direct and standardized assessment of sparse coder interpretability and compares scores with human evaluations across similar tasks.

papers.title: Evolution and compression in LLMs: on the emergence of human-aligned categorization
papers.contribution: Only models with strongest in-context capabilities recapitulate the wide range of near-optimal IB-tradeoffs observed in humans; other models converge to low-complexity solutions.

papers.title: Fantastic Reasoning Behaviors and Where to Find Them: Unsupervised Discovery of the Reasoning Process
papers.contribution: Discovers interpretable behaviors like reflection and backtracking with targeted interventions enabling controllable amplification or suppression of specific reasoning behaviors without retraining.

papers.title: Features Emerge as Discrete States: The First Application of SAEs to 3D Representations
papers.contribution: First SAE application to 3D domain reveals networks approximate discrete state space; explains unexpected phenomena including positional encoding preference and bimodal phase transitions.

papers.title: From Tokens to Thoughts: How LLMs and Humans Trade Compression for Meaning
papers.contribution: LLMs aggressively compress information achieving information-theoretic efficiency while humans prioritize contextual richness; encoder models outperform decoders in human alignment.

papers.title: GRADIEND: Feature Learning within Neural Networks Exemplified through Biases
papers.contribution: The approach demonstrates effectiveness across various model architectures in identifying bias-related features while maintaining other capabilities.

papers.title: Global Geometry Is Not Enough for Vision Representations
papers.contribution: Functional sensitivity reliably tracks compositional binding while geometry metrics fail; establishes functional sensitivity as critical complementary axis for modeling composite structure.

papers.title: How do LLMs Compute Verbal Confidence?
papers.contribution: Shows cached representations explain substantial variance beyond token log-probabilities, revealing a richer answer-quality evaluation than fluency readout, with implications for understanding LLM metacognition.

papers.title: I Predict Therefore I Am: Is Next Token Prediction Enough to Learn Human-Interpretable Concepts from Data?
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical evidence that LLMs capture essential generative factors, offers unified perspective on linear representation hypothesis, motivates sparse autoencoder evaluation.

papers.title: Inside the Visual Mind: Neuroscience-Motivated Concept Circuits for Interpreting and Steering Vision Transformers
papers.contribution: Improves concept coverage efficiency by 20x over ImageNet and interpretation accuracy by 28.7% over existing concept sets; concept editing improves worst-group accuracy on WaterBirds by 48.2%.

papers.title: Interpretability Transfer from Language to Vision via Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Achieves threefold increase in concept matching rate and enables fine-grained localized concept interventions with 35% improvement in object removal and 47% in object replacement.

papers.title: Interpretable Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders: A Data Analysis Toolkit
papers.contribution: SAE embeddings uncover semantic differences at 2-8x lower cost than LLMs and outperform dense embeddings on property-based retrieval through concept filtering.

papers.title: Interpreting Genomic Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: SAE features from intermediate layers are more interpretable than raw embeddings on 76% of genomic concept evaluations with 26/55 having F1 > 0.7.

papers.title: Is This Just Fantasy? Language Model Representations Reflect Human Judgments of Event Plausibility
papers.contribution: Shows LMs have more reliable modal categorization than previously reported and identifies a consistent emergence order of modal representations through training steps, layers, and model capacity.

papers.title: LABEL-FREE MITIGATION OF SPURIOUS CORRELATIONS IN VLMS USING SPARSE AUTOENCODERS
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms or matches existing baselines on spurious correlation benchmarks in terms of overall and worst-group accuracy without requiring auxiliary data or external supervision.

papers.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
papers.contribution: Empirically shows MLP neurons are as sparse a feature basis as SAEs; identifies circuits of ~100 neurons for subject-verb agreement and causal neurons for multi-hop reasoning without additional training costs.

papers.title: Latent Concept Disentanglement in Transformer-based Language Models
papers.contribution: Shows that both small and large models can disentangle and utilize latent concepts learned in-context from handful of abbreviated demonstrations.

papers.title: LatentLens: Revealing Highly Interpretable Visual Tokens in LLMs
papers.contribution: LatentLens shows that the majority of visual tokens are interpretable across all studied vision-language models and layers, providing more fine-grained interpretations than token-level analysis.

papers.title: Learning Self-Interpretation from Interpretability Artifacts: Training Lightweight Adapters on Vector-Label Pairs
papers.contribution: Generates sparse autoencoder feature labels outperforming training labels (70% versus 50% at 70B), identifies topics with 94% recall@1, decodes bridge entities in reasoning without chain-of-thought.

papers.title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
papers.contribution: Meta-model's learned prior improves steering intervention fluency; neurons isolate concepts with sparse probing scores scaling with model loss.

papers.title: Learning multimodal dictionary decompositions with group-sparse autoencoders
papers.contribution: Learns more multimodal dictionaries while reducing dead neurons and improving feature semanticity compared to standard SAEs.

papers.title: Med-SegLens: Latent-Level Model Diffing for Interpretable Medical Image Segmentation
papers.contribution: Identify latent features as causal bottlenecks for failures and show targeted interventions correct 70% of errors, improving Dice score from 39.4% to 74.2% without retraining.

papers.title: MetaOthello: A Controlled Study of Multiple World Models in Transformers
papers.contribution: Shows transformers learn shared world-state representations, resolve ambiguity through localized mechanisms, and structure representations abstractly beyond surface form.

papers.title: Narrow Finetuning Leaves Clearly Readable Traces in the Activation Differences
papers.contribution: ADL recovers the format and general content of finetuning data from activation differences and significantly enhances interpretability agents' ability to identify finetuning objectives.

papers.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection in Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Training on 10% selected Alpaca-GPT4 subset consistently outperforms methods using external models or uncertainty features across various tasks.

papers.title: On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy
papers.contribution: Reveals fundamental SAE limitations theoretically and demonstrates that reweighting significantly improves feature monosemanticity and interpretability.

papers.title: On the Predictive Power of Representation Dispersion in Language Models
papers.contribution: Measuring dispersion on unlabeled text predicts downstream accuracy in new domains, identifying high-dispersion layers improves retrieval methods, and a simple push-away objective directly improves perplexity.

papers.title: On the Relationship Between Activation Outliers and Feature Death in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Identifies dimension-level activation outliers as cause of feature death via initialization bias, providing principled basis for preprocessing.

papers.title: PolySAE: Modeling Feature Interactions in Sparse Autoencoders via Polynomial Decoding
papers.contribution: PolySAE improves probing F1 by ~8% while maintaining comparable reconstruction, produces 2-10x larger class-conditional feature distribution distances, and shows interaction weights exhibit negligible correlation with co-occurrence (r=0.06 vs r=0.82 for SAE).

papers.title: Priors in time: Missing inductive biases for language model interpretability
papers.contribution: Temporal SAE correctly parses garden path sentences, identifies event boundaries, and delineates abstract slow-moving from novel fast-moving information better than existing SAEs.

papers.title: Quantifying the Uncertainty of Foundation Models with Singular Value Ensembles
papers.contribution: SVE achieves comparable uncertainty estimation to explicit ensembles while increasing parameter count by <1%, making principled uncertainty estimation accessible for resource-constrained settings.

papers.title: Readout Representation: Redefining Neural Codes by Input Recovery
papers.contribution: Shows inputs can be accurately reconstructed from heavily perturbed mid-level features, challenging causal mapping perspectives and offering new lens for analyzing biological and artificial neural systems.

papers.title: Reasoning Compartmentalization: Bridging the Concretization Gap via Abstraction-based Routing
papers.contribution: Results suggest abstraction alleviates formulation sensitivity by strengthening connections between formulation-specific pathways rather than aligning representations.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning Enhances Activation Intensity and Diversity in the Internal Circuitry of LLMs
papers.contribution: Identifies two robust effects of online RL: increased average activation intensity and greater activation pattern diversity (higher entropy), suggesting RL makes information flow more redundant and flexible; DPO-trained models deviate from these trends.

papers.title: Revisiting Anisotropy in Language Transformers: The Geometry of Learning Dynamics
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical arguments assessing the problematic nature of anisotropy and observes geometric internal model dynamics across multiple models and checkpoints.

papers.title: RouterInterp: Understanding Superposed Specialisation in Mixture of Experts Routing
papers.contribution: RouterInterp explains expert routing with 57% higher detection accuracy than prior methods; demonstrates SSH better accounts for MoE routing behavior.

papers.title: SAE as a Crystal Ball: Interpretable Features Predict Cross-domain Transferability of LLMs without Training
papers.contribution: STS accurately predicts supervised fine-tuning transferability with Pearson correlation above 0.75 with actual performance changes, serving as an interpretable tool for guiding post-training strategies.

papers.title: SAEs-BrainMap: Unveiling the Emergence of Specialized Concepts in Deep Models via Brain Alignment
papers.contribution: Demonstrates robust representational alignment between sparse model features and biological ROIs, enables hierarchical trajectory tracing of generic concepts across layers using brain structure.

papers.title: SASFT: Sparse Autoencoder-guided Supervised Finetuning to Mitigate Unexpected Code-Switching in LLMs
papers.contribution: Reduces unexpected code-switching by over 50% with complete elimination in four cases, while maintaining or improving performance on six multilingual benchmarks.

papers.title: ST-TGExplainer: Disentangling Stability and Transition Patterns for Temporal GNN Interpretability
papers.contribution: Achieves strong predictive performance and yields more faithful temporal explanations by explicitly modeling both stability and transition patterns.

papers.title: SVD as a Fast Interpretability Method for Transformers
papers.contribution: Achieves orders-of-magnitude efficiency gains over training-based baselines while maintaining weight fidelity in identifying functional pathways.

papers.title: Signal in the Noise: Polysemantic Interference Transfers and Predicts Cross-Model Influence
papers.contribution: Counterintuitive interference patterns from small models reliably transfer to larger models (Llama-3.1, Gemma-2), yielding predictable behavioral shifts, suggesting convergent internal representations.

papers.title: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
papers.contribution: Only 30% of features are shared across seeds in a 131K-latent SAE; ReLU SAEs show greater stability while TopK SAEs are more seed-dependent, suggesting SAEs find pragmatic decompositions rather than true features.

papers.title: Sparse Autoencoders are Topic Models
papers.contribution: More coherent topics than baselines while maintaining diversity; enables large-scale thematic analysis across modalities without retraining.

papers.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Emotion Control in Text-to-Speech
papers.contribution: Sparse latent features achieve comparable or superior emotion induction and suppression relative to global steering, with distinct features associated with specific acoustic attributes.

papers.title: Sparse Relaxed-Lasso Steering: Automatic Sparse Autoencoder Feature Selection for Precise Image Editing
papers.contribution: Improves the alignment-consistency-quality trade-off over competing methods through automatic feature selection and optimized steering strength.

papers.title: Sparse but Wrong: Incorrect L0 Leads to Incorrect Features in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Most commonly used SAEs have L0 too low; practitioners must set L0 correctly to train monosemantic SAEs, with proxy metric helping find correct value on given distribution.

papers.title: Step-Level Sparse Autoencoder for Reasoning Process Interpretation
papers.contribution: Extracted features enable linear probing for both surface information (generation length, first token) and reasoning properties (correctness, logicality).

papers.title: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders: Leveraging the Sequential Nature of Language for Interpretability
papers.contribution: Recover smoother, more coherent semantic concepts without sacrificing reconstruction quality, exhibiting clear semantic structure without explicit semantic signal.

papers.title: The Geometry of Reasoning: Flowing Logics in Representation Space
papers.contribution: LLM reasoning corresponds to smooth flows whose velocities are locally controlled by logical statements, providing a geometric foundation and practical tools for interpretability analysis.

papers.title: The Price of Amortized inference in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Semi-amortized and non-amortized approaches significantly mitigate pathological phenomena like feature absorption and dead latents.

papers.title: The Tell-Tale Norm: $\ell_2$ Magnitude as a Signal for Reasoning Dynamics in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Proved L2 norm bounds SAE reasoning feature activations and showed norm-based techniques significantly improve reasoning across architectures and benchmarks.

papers.title: There Was Never a Bottleneck in Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.contribution: MCBMs yield more interpretable representations, support principled concept-level interventions, and remain consistent with probability-theoretic foundations.

papers.title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Achieve lower reconstruction error and improved stability in sparse autoencoders with theoretical grounding through dictionary learning connections.

papers.title: Uncovering Conceptual Blindspots in Generative Image Models Using Sparse Autoencoders
papers.contribution: Identifies specific suppressed blindspots (bird feeders, DVD discs, whitespaces) and exaggerated blindspots (wood texture, palm trees) across four popular models, plus memorization artifacts.

papers.title: What Do Large Language Models Know About Opinions?
papers.contribution: Shows internal knowledge of opinions exceeds output knowledge with 50-59% improvement, competitive to fine-tuning but 278× less computationally expensive.
